title: Reading the scenario and the people list
blurb: Pull the deciding facts out of the scenario booklet and match people to roles and influence from their backgrounds, not their job titles.
question: The people list names twelve people with one-line backgrounds. A question asks who is best suited to be the chief product owner, and another asks who is the key influencer for passengers. What exactly are you looking for?

teach.h: Read the booklet like an investigator
teach.body: The scenario booklet sets the scene: the organization, the project, its fixed points, its teams and its tensions. Each question then adds its own short situation. You are not reading for the story; you are hunting for the facts that decide answers. The 'Additional information (People)' section matters too: at least one question needs it, usually to match a person to a role or to spot who has influence.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile Practitioner syllabus v2.0, exam overview

teach.h: A first read in four passes

steps.label: People list
steps.sub: Pencil a likely role beside each

teach.body: A stakeholder is anyone who can affect, be affected by, or believes they are affected by the change. Key influencers are the people who shape how the majority sees the change and, through their networks, most influence whether it is adopted and benefits are realized. Look for credibility and a network among the people who must adopt the change, not seniority, budget or technical skill.

teach.body: Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares app only pays off if passengers use it. The people list includes Bronwen Hale (commercial director, holds the budget), Gemma Lowther (Coinbridge account director) and Nigel Ormsby (chair of the 30-member passenger panel, a daily commuter). The key influencer for passengers is Nigel: he has a network and credibility among the people who must adopt the app. Bronwen is senior and Gemma is the supplier, but neither shapes how passengers see the change.

teach.h: Where does the answer come from?

children.label: Use that fact for this question

children.edge: It names a person or role
children.label: Check the people list

teach.text: Three people-list traps. The most senior person is rarely the key influencer: look for network and credibility among the adopters. A 'Scrum master' fits the team coach role, not project manager or agile coach. And a person who manages one team's backlog fits product owner; the chief product owner sets priorities across all the teams.

items: Hunt for fixed points, teams, contracts, maturity, tensions and affected people.
The people list is needed for at least one question, usually role fit or influence.
Match backgrounds to role descriptions; job titles can mislead.
Key influencer = network and credibility with adopters, not seniority.
Each question stands alone: its own situation wins for that question.

summary: You can now read a scenario booklet for the facts that decide answers and use the people list to match backgrounds to PRINCE2 Agile roles. You can also identify stakeholders and key influencers in a scenario.

A.q: Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project has three delivery teams. Candidates for chief product owner are: Matteo Ricci, head of digital products, who sets direction for all digital channels and works with users and the passenger panel; Sasha Ellery, who has written and prioritized the app team's stories for three years; Priyanka Desai, an agile lead who coaches departments and senior managers; and Owen Thackeray, the app team's Scrum master. Who is best suited to the role?
A.why: The CPO represents the user community, owns the project backlog and sets priorities across teams; Matteo already sets direction across all digital channels and works with users.

whyNot.0: Sasha's background fits the product owner of one team, not priorities across three teams.
whyNot.1: A Scrum master fits the team coach role.
whyNot.2: Priyanka's coaching of departments and leaders fits the agile coach role.

A.q: Larkspur Rail needs passengers to trust and use the new delay compensation features in its app. The project manager wants one person to help shape passengers' views of the change. The people list includes Bronwen Hale, the commercial director who holds the budget; Gemma Lowther, account director at the payments supplier; Nigel Ormsby, chair of the passenger panel and a daily commuter; and Fatima Zahra, head of data. Who is the key influencer for passengers?
A.why: Key influencers shape the perception of the majority through their networks (4.2.2); Nigel has standing and a network among passengers.

whyNot.0: Bronwen is senior and holds the budget, but she does not shape how passengers see the change.
whyNot.2: The supplier's account director has no network among passengers.
whyNot.3: Fatima is a technical specialist leading the data team, not a voice among passengers.

A.q: Larkspur Rail's board has said the £3.2 million budget and December end date for Fair Fares cannot move. Midway through Stage 3, the app team's burn-up shows that not all the Release 2 stories will be finished by the planned release date. Which action is MOST LIKELY to be appropriate?
options: Ask the board for one more month to finish every story
Ask the board for extra budget to bring in a contractor team
Release the Must haves and drop the lowest-priority Could haves
Shorten testing on Release 2 so that all stories fit
A.why: Time and cost have zero tolerance in PRINCE2 Agile; scope flexes for Should and Could haves (Table 3.1).

whyNot.0: The booklet fixes the end date; time has zero tolerance.
whyNot.1: The booklet fixes the £3.2 million budget, and cost has zero tolerance.
whyNot.3: Cutting testing lowers quality rather than flexing lower-priority scope.

B.q: Larkspur Rail's app team needs a team coach for Fair Fares. The people list includes Priyanka Desai, an agile lead in IT who has coached several departments and senior managers; Owen Thackeray, the team's Scrum master, who facilitates its sprint events and retrospectives; Sasha Ellery, who writes and prioritizes the team's stories; and Rhys Pengelly, an experienced PRINCE2 project manager. Who is best suited to the team coach role?
B.why: The team coach works closely with one or two teams, helps them self-manage and facilitates team workshops; a Scrum master fits this role.

whyNot.0: Priyanka's organization-wide coaching of leaders fits the agile coach role.
whyNot.2: Rhys's background fits the project manager role.
whyNot.3: Sasha's backlog work fits the product owner role.

B.q: Callowmere University is creating a single Student Support Hub, and wellbeing staff must change how they take referrals. The people list includes Dr Kwame Mensah, director of the 45-strong wellbeing service; Tom Brierley, an experienced adviser who is respected by colleagues and openly doubtful about the hub; Maya Kowalczyk, the students' union welfare officer; and Sinead Walsh, an independent quality manager. Who is the key influencer for wellbeing staff?
B.why: A key influencer shapes the views of the majority through their network (4.2.2); Tom is respected by the staff who must adopt the change.

whyNot.1: Kwame is the most senior, but seniority is not the test; network and credibility among adopters is.
whyNot.2: Maya influences students, not wellbeing staff.
whyNot.3: Sinead is independent of the service, so she is not part of the staff's network.

B.q: Larkspur Rail's booklet says the app team's velocity has ranged from 18 to 34 story points over six sprints. A question then states that over the last three sprints the team completed 22, 20 and 21 points, and asks how many more sprints the remaining 126 points of Release 3 will take at that rate. What is the answer?
B.why: The question gives its own recent velocity: an average of 21 points, so 126 / 21 = 6 sprints. Use the question's facts for that question.

whyNot.0: 4 sprints uses the booklet's best sprint of 34 points, not the question's own data.
whyNot.1: 5 sprints uses the midpoint of the booklet's range (26), not the question's own data.
whyNot.2: 7 sprints uses the booklet's worst sprint of 18 points, not the question's own data.

C.q: On Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project, the head of customer relations fears automatic payment will increase fraud and change her 40 staff's jobs. The project manager invites her to every progress review demo and asks a claims adviser respected by her colleagues to help test each release. Is this an appropriate way to work with these stakeholders, and why?
options: Yes, because involving affected staff and influencers helps adoption
Yes, because the head of customer relations owns the benefits
No, because demos are held for the delivery team and the CPO
No, because fears about job changes belong in the risk register
C.why: Agile supports OCM through user involvement, frequent testing and demos at progress reviews, and working with key influencers among the affected groups (4.2.2, 4.2.4).

whyNot.1: Benefits sit with the business case and the executive; this is not why her involvement is right.
whyNot.2: Progress review demos are a chance to gather acceptance and feedback from users and stakeholders.
whyNot.3: A related risk may be recorded, but that does not make involving affected staff wrong.

C.q: Larkspur Rail's project manager proposes Priyanka Desai as team coach for the app team, because she is the most experienced agile person in the company. Priyanka is an agile lead in IT who has coached several departments and senior managers. Owen Thackeray is the app team's Scrum master. Is this an appropriate choice, and why?
options: Yes, because a team coach needs the most agile experience
Yes, because a team coach can support one or two teams
No, because a Scrum master cannot hold a PRINCE2 Agile role
No, because her background fits the agile coach role better
C.why: The agile coach works across the organization, coaches leaders and removes systemic blockers; the team coach works inside one or two teams, which a Scrum master like Owen fits.

whyNot.0: Role fit depends on what the role does, not on seniority or years of experience.
whyNot.1: True that a team coach supports one or two teams, but it does not explain why Priyanka fits.
whyNot.2: A Scrum master fits the team coach role well.

C.q: The Larkspur Rail booklet says the end date cannot move. One question states that the board has since agreed a two-week extension for Release 3 after a regulator's request, and asks what the project manager should update. Ruth decides to answer as if the extension had not happened. Is this an appropriate reading, and why?
options: Yes, because booklet facts outrank the facts in a question
Yes, because time has zero tolerance in PRINCE2 Agile
No, because the question's situation sets the context for it
No, because the booklet is not used in any question
C.why: Each question adds its own situation and is answered on its own; the stem's facts apply to that question.

whyNot.0: The question's own situation is the context the examiner wants you to use.
whyNot.1: Zero time tolerance is the default, but the stem states the board has decided an extension.
whyNot.3: The booklet is used; at least one question needs the people list.

reteach.title: Read like a detective, not a reader
reteach.question: A detective reads a witness list for who could have done it. What should you read the people list for?

blocks.body: A detective ignores job titles and asks what each person actually does and who they know. Do the same: what decisions does this person make, whose priorities do they set, and who listens to them? Those three answers place almost everyone in the right role.

items: Read what the person does, not what they are called.
Match it to the role description.
For influence, ask who the adopters listen to.

explain.body: A stakeholder is any individual, group or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceives itself to be affected by the change.

test.q: Larkspur Rail's 40 customer relations staff are not on any Fair Fares team, but their work checking claims will change once compensation is paid through the app. How should the project regard them?
options: As key influencers, since their jobs will change
As project assurance, since they check claims
As stakeholders, since the change affects them
As users outside the scope of the project
test.why: Anyone affected by the change is a stakeholder, whether or not they work on the project (4.2.2).

whyNot.0: Being affected makes them stakeholders; key influencers are those with network influence over adopters.
whyNot.1: Project assurance independently monitors the project for the board; checking claims is their day job.
whyNot.3: People affected by the change are stakeholders to be engaged, not outside the project's concern.

explain.body: The product owner is a version of the team manager: owns one team's product backlog, prepares and maintains its user stories and agrees work packages with the project manager.

test.q: In Larkspur Rail's people list, Sasha Ellery is a senior product manager who has written and prioritized the user stories for the app team for three years. Which PRINCE2 Agile role best fits her background?
options: Product owner for the app team
Chief product owner for the project
Team coach for the app team
test.why: Writing and prioritizing one team's stories is the product owner's work on the product backlog.

whyNot.1: The CPO sets priorities across all the teams and owns the project backlog.
whyNot.2: The team coach helps the team self-manage; it does not own the backlog.
whyNot.3: Project support provides administration and dashboard support.

explain.body: The tester designs, runs and may automate tests, and reviews products against acceptance criteria and the team's Definition of Done.

test.q: Hollie Brennan is a test automation engineer in Larkspur Rail's app team. She writes automated tests and checks stories against their acceptance criteria. Which PRINCE2 Agile role best fits her?
test.why: Designing and automating tests and checking against acceptance criteria is the tester role.

whyNot.0: Project assurance monitors adherence to principles and governance for the board, not story testing.
whyNot.1: Developers design, build and maintain the increments.
whyNot.2: The team coach helps the team self-manage and facilitates its workshops.

explain.body: How procurement and contracts support agile delivery, for example a fixed team cost per iteration or an agreed Definition of Done, is set out in the commercial management approach in the organization practice.

test.q: Larkspur Rail's booklet says Coinbridge Payments works under a fixed-price contract, and any scope change will need a formal variation. In initiation, the project manager wants to record how this contract will be managed alongside agile delivery. Where should this be recorded?
options: In the project management team structure
test.why: The commercial management approach covers procurement, the delivery model and contract management, and should support agile working (7.3.2).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions set out individual responsibilities, not contract arrangements.
whyNot.2: The communication management approach covers how information flows to and from stakeholders.
whyNot.3: The team structure shows who is involved and how they work together, not the contract terms.
